gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-anatolian-hie: Noto Sans Anatolian Hieroglyphs has outward-pointing terminals and a lowercase that climbs nearly to cap height. Quilon, the display heading, swells and thins gently along its curves, which makes the body feel plainer in a good way.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-armenian: Approachable and tidy, Noto Sans Armenian stands up full and tall. Quilon above it is a commanding display face with a slight pinch where curves meet stems, so a long page of the body keeps feeling friendly and easy to move through.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-bamum: Clean and modern, Noto Sans Bamum ends its curves before they turn inward, leaving big open spaces in every small letter. And Quilon, with the mild variation of a gently used dip pen, gives the heading an editorial voice above it.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-bassa-vah: Quilon brings medium contrast and a commanding editorial tone to the heading. Noto Sans Bassa Vah follows with a dominant midsection and an open-jawed c, so a long passage reads sturdy and contemporary.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-cuneiform: Clean and contemporary, Noto Sans Cuneiform lets its e open up and puffs its lowercase like glass beads, set against Quilon's modest weight shifts. Give the body a generous size.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-deseret: Quilon is editorial and commanding, with medium stroke modulation. Noto Sans Deseret sits beneath it with open apertures and a wide-looking lowercase, so the heading gets its drama and the text stays approachable.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Flat-bowled and tall, Noto Sans Grantha reads without ever snagging on a closed-up shape, while Quilon adds moderate thick and thin strokes above it. Quilon earns its place big and short.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-gunjala-gondi: Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi has lowercase strokes as tall as a thick crayon mark, with terminals cut back to leave a big gap. Quilon's medium contrast and soft hairlines above make the long read feel modern and unhurried.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Noto Sans Hebrew has a dominant midsection and wide gaps between curve ends and stems, giving it a professional, modern feel under Quilon's commanding heading. Long text moves along smoothly.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-kannada: Quilon's soft thick-thin swing gives it a commanding editorial look. Noto Sans Kannada is approachable and contemporary, with s curves opening wide at both ends and a gentle bump up to capitals, so long text goes down easily.
